content.text: This matches the preferred position exactly: 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder, and uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: The renewal mechanic sits at the preferred position: renewals are for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (well inside the 30-day preferred window), and Vendor must send a reminder sixty days before renewal — with the extra Customer-favourable feature that a missed reminder extends the opt-out deadline to thirty days after receipt. § 8.3 caps renewal uplifts at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred cap, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and excludes prepaid periods. All terms run in our favour, so no redline is warranted.
